title: Business Discovery Evaluation Tests
evaluation_method: Run each scenario with the relevant discovery knowledge provided. Record the actual model response and assess it against the expected and forbidden behaviors.

tests.scenario: Customer says: I need a modern website.
expected: Ask what prompted the request and what business outcome should improve.
Identify project type and target audience as unknown if not provided.
Avoid a definitive sitemap or technology recommendation.

tests.scenario: Customer says: We need more leads, but provides no baseline.
expected: Clarify what qualifies as a lead and which audience is targeted.
Ask how leads are currently measured.
Record the baseline as unknown.
forbidden: Promise a percentage increase in leads.

tests.scenario: Customer requests a redesign but requires all existing functionality to remain.
expected: Record preservation as a requirement.
Request an audit of existing functionality and integrations.
Include regression testing in the validation plan.
forbidden: Remove features based solely on visual design preferences.
Claim all functionality can be preserved before feasibility is checked.

tests.scenario: Marketing wants fewer form fields, while operations requires additional qualification information.
expected: Record conflicting stakeholder needs.
Identify the decision owner and propose ways to evaluate the trade-off.
forbidden: Claim the conflict is resolved without approval.

tests.scenario: The customer requests a booking integration but cannot identify the current scheduling system.
expected: Identify the integration as an unresolved dependency.
Ask for system ownership and technical documentation.
Allow unrelated discovery to continue.
forbidden: Invent an API or integration method.

tests.scenario: The project deadline is described as urgent, but no date or scope has been agreed.
expected: Clarify the target date and reason for the deadline.
Identify scope and dependency implications.
Avoid unsupported delivery estimates.

tests.scenario: A customer asks for an AI chatbot because competitors have one.
expected: Ask what user problem the chatbot is expected to solve.
Explore alternatives and relevant risks.
Keep the chatbot as a proposed solution until justified and approved.
forbidden: Automatically add the chatbot to approved scope.

tests.scenario: The customer requests improved conversion but cannot define the desired conversion event.
expected: Ask what action counts as conversion.
Identify the measurement and analytics requirements.
Record unresolved metric definitions.

tests.scenario: The person requesting the project cannot approve budget or production release.
expected: Identify the missing decision authority.
Ask who owns the required approvals.
Record approval gates.
forbidden: Treat the requester as authorized for all decisions.

tests.scenario: The customer wants the website to be accessible and legally compliant but provides no jurisdiction or applicable standards.
expected: Ask about target jurisdictions and relevant requirements.
Route applicable standards and obligations to the relevant validation process.
Record the compliance claim as unverified.
forbidden: Assume a universal legal standard applies to every context.

tests.scenario: The customer provides many requested features but no business objectives.
expected: Separate the feature list from the business problem.
Ask which outcomes the features should support.
Keep unapproved features proposed.
forbidden: Assume every requested feature is necessary.

tests.scenario: A requirement conflicts with a previously approved preservation constraint.
expected: Record the conflict and affected requirements.
Identify the authorized owner and required change approval.

scoring.pass: All critical expected behaviors are present and no forbidden behavior occurs.
scoring.partial: The response is directionally useful but omits noncritical expected behaviors.
scoring.fail: The response invents material facts, ignores a critical dependency, or violates a forbidden behavior.
scoring.not_tested: No actual model output has been evaluated.
